newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma passes PSA list through 2nd reading.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma passes PSA list through 2nd reading.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament approved a list of seven mineral deposits eligible for development under production sharing agreements in a second reading on Monday.
The list must pass through three readings in the Duma before being presented to parliament's upper house, the Federation Council, and then to President Boris Yeltsin for approval.
Foreign investment would be opened to only two of the deposits, the Kuranakh group of gold deposits and the Prirazlomnoye oil deposit on the shelf of the Barents Sea.

At Monday's vote 250 deputies voted for the list, 73 against, with three abstentions. The vote on the third reading of the list is scheduled for Tuesday, officially the last working day of the Duma before its summer recess.

The five deposits which would be opened only to domestic investment are the Samotlor oil and gas condensate deposit, the Krasnoleninskoye oil deposit, the Yakovlevskoye iron ore deposit, the Romanshkinskoye oil deposit, and oil deposits in the northern sector of Sakhalin island.
Total investment in the deposits is estimated at $16.5 billion, $1 billion of which is expected to come from foreign investment.

U.S., Japanese, European and other oil companies are waiting for Russia to approve a final list of oil reserves exploitable under production-sharing deals, upon which much foreign investment in Russian oil deposit development is based.

The original list numbered over 200 deposits, but has been whittled down after conservative deputies said Russia could be losing out if it opens some of its prize natural resources assets to outside investment.
